html:
Maputo, the capital of Mozambique, grew from a small Portuguese trading post on Delagoa Bay into the colonial capital in 1898, under the name Lourenço Marques.

Its growth came from the Witwatersrand gold rush. A railway to Pretoria opened in 1895, and the port became a main outlet for the Transvaal, with Mozambican mine workers travelling the other way. It was a modern city of avenues, cafés and Portuguese settlers.

At independence in 1975 it was renamed Maputo. Most Portuguese left. It suffered during the civil war and has grown fast since, the political and business heart of Mozambique.
sum: Maputo, the capital of Mozambique, grew from a small Portuguese trading post on Delagoa Bay into the colonial capital in 1898, under the name Lourenço Marques.
